item.title: Korean Data Center Firm Elice Jumps by Limit After Debut Slump
item.description: South Korean AI computing supplier Elice Inc. surged on Wednesday, recovering much of the ground lost after a 32% slump in its trading debut, as a string of upbeat US tech earnings lifted sentiment.

item.title: Citi's Luet Sees AI Infrastructure Theme Continuing
item.description: Citi's Japan, Asia North and Australia Cluster and Banking Head Marc Luet expects AI infrastructure investment to remain a dominant theme, despite growing scrutiny. He speaks after data center firm Nextdc shares plunged following a public backlash. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: CATL’s Slower Profit Growth Fans Fears for China Battery Rivals
item.description: Battery giant Contemporary Amperex Technology Co. Ltd.’s slower-than-expected quarterly profit growth has prompted analysts to warn that the company and its peers may struggle to manage pressure from a revived domestic consumption tax and the end of other fiscal benefits.

item.title: Gold Steadies as Conflicting Iran Signals Cloud Path for Rates
item.description: Gold held a decline as conflicting signals on efforts to end the Iran war clouded the outlook for inflation and the Federal Reserve’s path for interest rates.

item.title: AI Stocks Rally After Super Micro Preliminary Sales Bring Relief
item.description: The shares of AI-related companies rallied in after-hours trading on Tuesday after strong preliminary results from server-maker Super Micro Computer Inc. spurred relief about the outlook for spending on the technology.

item.title: Asian Shares, US Futures Rise on AI-Trade Revival: Markets Wrap
item.description: Asian shares rose along with US equity-index futures as strong earnings from some of the biggest beneficiaries of the artificial intelligence boom revived optimism over the tech trade.

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Oct. 21
item.description: Oil edged higher as attacks on ships around the Strait of Hormuz threatened shipments, while US industry data pointed to another drop in stockpiles.

item.title: Netflix Sales Growth to Decline for Fourth Quarter in a Row
item.description: Netflix reported earnings for the third quarter that exceeded Wall Street expectations, but forecast a fourth consecutive quarter of slowing sales growth, a projection that may amplify concerns about the performance of the world’s leading online TV network. Netflix delivered sales of $12.9 billion in the third quarter, in line with Wall Street’s expectations, and forecast sales of $13.4 billion in the year’s final three months, falling short of what analysts have predicted. The pace of growth has fallen from 17.6% in the final quarter of last year to a projection of 11.5% for this year’s fourth quarter. The company blamed its sales shortfall on the advertising business, which is on pace to deliver $300 million less than the company expected. Bloomberg Tech Host Ed Ludlow joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss. He speaks with Alexis Christoforous and Norah Mulinda. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Surprising Netflix Is Not Looking at Other Opportunities: Fmr. Content Director
item.description: Simon Gallagher, Hanaging Director of SPG Global and a Former Netflix Content-Acquisition Director, says hiring Peter Rice signals a more commercial programming strategy. While niche titles can succeed, Gallagher argues Netflix should lean more toward broadly appealing films and shows to support growth. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: PGIM’s Bryan McDonnell on 2027 Real Estate Credit Market
item.description: Bryan McDonnell, Head of Real Estate Credit Strategies at PGIM, says investors should adjust business models to a higher-rate environment rather than count on rates falling. He describes the market’s recent uncertainty as a gap between rate expectations and reality, with Treasury yields rising above 5% after expectations briefly converged around 4%. He speaks with Romaine Bostick & Jess Menton on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: United Misses Estimates, Squeezed by Soaring Jet Fuel Costs
item.description: United Airlines Holdings Inc. forecast weaker-than-expected earnings for the final three months of the year, underscoring how soaring jet fuel prices are eating into airline profits despite resilient demand for air travel.

item.title: Brazil Readies China Bond Debut for as Soon as Next Week
item.description: Brazil is readying its debut panda-bond sale, which could take place as early as next week, according to a person familiar with the matter.

item.title: Lithium Miner PLS Sells $700 Million Bond in Expansion Push
item.description: PLS Group Ltd returned to the US dollar bond market, braving a junk-debt selloff as the Australian lithium miner lines up investments to expand production.

item.title: Top Chicken Supplier Brazil Acts to Ease Hit From Virus
item.description: Brazil raced to contain the trade fallout from the detection of a highly contagious bird virus as poultry shipments to countries including top buyer China faced restrictions.

item.title: S&P 500 Climbs as Big Bank Stocks Rally, SpaceX Results Loom
item.description: The S&P 500 Index erased early-session losses to close higher on Tuesday as big banks and healthcare companies rallied. The tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 Index ended the day with a slight decline after South Korean neocloud company Elice Inc. tanked in its trading debut, spurring concern about the sustainability of the global AI boom.

item.title: Stocks Climb in Late Hours After SpaceX’s Earnings: Markets Wrap
item.description: Stocks rose in late hours as SpaceX reported solid earnings fueled by a big jump in its artificial-intelligence business.

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Oct. 20
item.description: Brent oil edged lower in a choppy session, with traders parsing the status of negotiations between the US and Iran against a backdrop of persistent unrest in the Middle East.

item.title: Latin American Trump Allies Embrace Washington Lenders
item.description: Latin America’s rightward, market-friendly shift is reshaping its relationship with Donald Trump’s Washington, including new flows of money from the multilateral lenders historically villainized in the region for pushing fiscal austerity.

item.title: Brazil Election: Bolsonaro Says He’d Work With US, China as President
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro said he would work with the US and China if he becomes Brazil’s president, after a surprise election performance left him poised to join a wave of conservative leaders pushing Latin America closer to Washington.

item.title: South America’s Right-Wing Shift Has Reached Brazil
item.description: Brazil’s presidential runoff is shaping up as an opportunity for the political right to cement its power across South America.
